chunks: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:

When the servant is in the last day of this world and the first day of the Hereafter, his wealth, his children, and his deeds are made to appear before him. He turns to his wealth and says: By Allah, I was surely eager and miserly concerning you, so what do you have for me? It says: Take from me your shroud. Then he turns to his children and says: By Allah, I surely loved you, and I was surely protective over you, so what do you have for me? They say: We will deliver you to your grave and bury you in it. Then he turns to his deeds and says: By Allah, you were surely burdensome upon me, and I was surely disinclined toward you, so what do you have for me? It says: I am your companion in your grave and on the day of your gathering, until I and you are presented before your Lord.

key_terms.حَشْرِكَ: the gathering on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.عَمَلُهُ: one's deeds, which remain as the true lasting companion
key_terms.قَبْرِكَ: the grave, where the servant is accompanied by his deeds
key_terms.مَالُهُ: one's wealth, which only benefits to the extent of burial provision
key_terms.وُلْدُهُ: one's children, who accompany him only to burial
key_terms.ٱلدُّنْيَا: the present worldly life that comes to an end at death
key_terms.ٱلْآخِرَةِ: the next world that begins for the person after death
key_terms.ٱلْعَبْدَ: the human servant standing before the transition from worldly life to the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What stays with a person after death according to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that at the threshold of the Hereafter, a person's wealth and children can only accompany him to limited stages, while his deeds remain with him in the grave and until presentation before Allah. It emphasizes the enduring consequence of one's actions and warns against excessive attachment to worldly possessions and relations over righteous deeds.
